asr.full_text: I used to waste 3 hours editing a 15 second clip. I'd open some AI video tool. Stare at a giant, empty prompt box. A cockpit timeline I didn't understand. A list of model names nobody asked me to memorize. And just ... close the tab. Sound familiar? That's not your problem. That's a broken workflow problem. And I think I found something that actually fixes it. It's called Pexo AI. It's in Beta right now and it completely flips how you make videos. Not type a perfect prompt and pray. You just talk to it. Like texting a friend! Let's dive in! Why do all the AI use Open Claw? Here's where it gets interesting. I connected Pexo to Open Claw. Which means it lives right inside the chat apps I already use. Whatsapp, Telegram, Discord. No new tab, no new app. I opened a Discord chat and typed, hey, I want a vertical AI video, around 30 seconds, showing a futuristic desk set up for a productivity reel with chill music. That's the whole message. A few moments later, Pexo dropped a finished clip right back into the same thread. And then I just replied, make the camera move smoother, slow the pacing a bit, try a more ambient soundtrack, new version, same thread. The whole creative workflow happens inside one conversation. No timeline scrubbing, no dragging clips around, no exporting to another tool. Now, if you want to see what's actually happening under the hood, the Pexo Web Dashboard is where it gets really cool. You can watch the behind the scenes dialogue between OpenCla and Pexo in real time. How they break down your request, which AI models they pick for each scene, how creative decisions get made. It's not a blackbox where you wait and hope. You see the plan before anything gets rendered. Of course, you can also jump straight into the Pexo web app. That's where you get the full experience with every think it can do. I tested this with a product ad scenario. I told it in plain language, I need a nine by 16 video under a minute that feels like a user generated ad for a mechanical keyboard, casual tone, quick cuts, upbeat music, text on screen highlighting features, Pexo immediately started thinking out loud on the dashboard. It broke the idea into scenes, proposed a structure, suggested visual styles, and showed different, quick previews. Hookshot, close up, feature text, pop. And if I didn't like something, I didn't restart. I just said, make the opening shot more close up on the keys, and it adjusted on the fly. They call this editing without the editing, and that's exactly what it feels like. On the web preview, you can circle a specific frame, leave a comment like you would in a Google doc, and Pexo fixes just that part. In my keyboard ad, one shot had flat lighting. I circled it, wrote more dramatic, stronger contrast on the keys. Done! No redescribing the whole scene. And it doesn't stop at a single clip. Through the same conversation you can continue the video with new scenes, split it for different platforms, add voiceover, subtitles, change the music, adjust pacing, restyle transitions, generate thumbnails, and cover art. Full creative workflow all in chat. Under the hood it auto-select from top models like Sea Dance, Cling and others depending on what each scene actually needs. You never have to think about which model is best for what. Quick Specs, videos up to around two minutes per run, horizontal, vertical and square formats and you can chain them together with the Continuation feature for longer content. Free Tier gives you a solid amount of Credits when you sign-up, and you can earn more by sharing. It's in beta so you need a Gmail and an invite code to get in. My invite link and code are at the very top of the description. Use that, and you'll land on the aweb dashboard where you can see the full two AI workflows. Connect PXO to OpenClaw and start making videos straight from your chat apps. If my codes are gone check the official Pexo Discord. Also linked for more invites and updates. If you've been putting off video because editing is a nightmare this is the thing that removes that barrier. You don't need to know editing, you don't need prompt engineering, you don't need to care about models... if you can text a friend, you can use this. Drop a comment below with how you'd use it. Seriously I want to know product ads, youtube content, social clips, what's your use case? Hit subscribe so you don't miss the next deep dive and I'll see you in the next one.
